To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the existence of a regulatory body in a cluster significantly affects the emergence of both, inbound and outbound open innovations, by member firms in a cluster initiative, (2) this effect is moderated by trust and information asymmety, and (3) the effect is stronger for outbound open innovations than for inbound ones.
“A regulatory body in a cluster initiative increases open innovation culture of firms through increased effects of relational elements, i.e. trust and information asymmtry, in the cluster.”
a regulatory body of a cluster initiative can positively affect the open innovation behavior of its member firms by increasing the effects of trust and reducing information asymmetries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the institutionalization of a cluster initiative affects the open innovation activities within a cluster.
the question of what factors influence the emergence of open innovation in clusters.
the question of how cluster institutions influence open innovation activities of firms in a cluster.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a cluster initiative with a regulatory body can be considered as a facilitator of trust and information exchange, which in turn increases the openness of firms in the cluster.
a cluster initiative with an active regulatory body is more likely to foster open innovation culture than a cluster initiative without an active regulatory body.
the cluster initiative has been able to successfully establish a culture of open innovation among the members of the initiative, but not among the non members.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the establishment of a cluster initiative is not sufficient to promote open innovation.
a regulatory body of a cluster initiative can facilitate the development of an open innovation culture in a cluster.

the establishment of open innovation culture in clusters is facilitated by the presence of an institutionalized regulatory body, which increases trust between firms in the cluster and thereby reduces information asymmetries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the role of trust and asymmetry of information in the context of open innovation culture needs to be further investigated.
cluster organizations can facilitate open innovation culture in their member firms by creating a regulatory framework that fosters trust and reduces information asymmetry between cluster firms.
the role of a regulatory body in a cluster initiative can be used as a means to promote the open innovation culture in a cluster.
